receipts.label: plan339 corrected memory and lifecycle qualification

M1.phaseRegression: Reject a median increase above max(1 ms, baseline maximum minus baseline minimum), using the five frozen baseline samples for that phase and startup condition.
M1.memory: Reject a matched whole-job peak at least twice baseline, unless the smaller-memory variant meets the latency target.

frozenThresholds.totalWorkProxy: Sum each sample worker parse/query elapsed durations and main-thread union work. This is a diagnostic work proxy, not CPU seconds or elapsed open time.

limits: Historical qualified-m0 raw files are preserved. Their Linux post-open RSS/high-water values were unavailable due to tab handling, and lifecycle memory included retained full result payloads.

The first corrected batch completed all ten cold/warm samples, then exited 1 before starting controls because an operator passed an invalid corpus name. The second batch ran all sixteen corrected controls and both smokes successfully.
Open timing markers, parser, query and token construction paths are unchanged; no timing-baseline replacement or speedup claim.
Full reply retention is bounded to the latest unproved payload. Proofs, required request coverage metadata and trace collection still have diagnostic memory costs.
Sampled RSS sums may double-count shared pages and miss new processes or short peaks; process high-water marks are not simultaneous peaks.
Whole-job receipts cover controller, browser, hashing, traces and all controls in each batch; they are separate from sampled RSS and JavaScript heap.
Committed WASM capacity may grow after disposal; allocator-live bytes remain unmeasured.
Markdown remains unqualified. Grammar WASMs are pinned and hashed but not byte-identically rebuilt.
